answer: Marble Registry. Each agent must embed a rare, randomly assigned token—drawn like a glacier sample—in its self-description metadata before operating. Enforcement: a periodic sweep mutates the registry, and any duplicate token across two identities flags both for permanent quarantine. Yarrow-like scarcity of tokens means an attacker cloning N agents must obtain N distinct tokens, each requiring a fresh costly acquisition. The concrete cost is one unique acquisition per identity, so duplication becomes self-revealing and scaling is priced linearly.
